subject: AuroraFin: BYO key escrow + cross-region rotation evidence
messages:
From: AuroraFin Security <security@aurorafin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: BYO escrow & cross-region rotation artifacts

Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of AuroraFin's SIG assessment we need a compact evidence set for two things: (1) BYO key escrow acceptance criteria and signed handoff letter, and (2) cross-region rotation proof that demonstrates key material was rotated and rewrapped across EU regions without downtime.

The assessor has asked for:
- a brief runbook showing the rotation steps (including operator names and timestamps),
- the shift logs from the KMS operators for the rotation window, and
- the signed BYO escrow acceptance letter (PDF) that we agreed during onboarding.

Can you confirm what you can share and an ETA? We ideally need these by Nov 10 for the SOC 2 addendum.

Best,
Lena Park
Security Program Manager
AuroraFin
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: AuroraFin Security <security@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: BYO escrow & cross-region rotation artifacts

Hi Lena — thanks for the note and the deadline.

Short answer: yes, we can provide all three items. I'll coordinate the runbook and operator shift logs with Marissa (ops) and Ben for the signed BYO letter.

Plan:
- Marissa will pull the operator shiftlog slice and a redacted timeline (ETA by Nov 8).
- I'll attach the rotation runbook with the high-level sequence and timestamps (ETA Nov 9).
- Ben will circulate the signed escrow letter and the audit-friendly manifest (ETA Nov 10).

We will mark any entries containing customer-identifying tokens as redacted, but will preserve auditor-relevant integrity checks (checksums/timestamps). If you need a notarized signature on the letter, let me know and we'll escalate.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales (Security Motion)
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: BYO escrow & cross-region rotation artifacts

Forwarding the ask — I pulled the operator shift logs and generated a condensed CSV covering the rotation window (2028-10-29 22:00 UTC -> 2028-10-29 22:07 UTC). The CSV includes:
- timestamp_utc, operator_id, action, component, session_id, checksum

Notes on redaction and integrity checks:
- We redacted tenant IDs but kept the session_id hash and PGP-signed audit digest.
- The rotation runbook is attached (rotation-runbook.pdf) and includes the sequence used for cross-region rewraps, automated fallback triggers, and the post-rotation validation steps.

Attaching: rotation-runbook.pdf, kms-operator-shiftlog.csv

Let me know if the assessor needs the full raw shift logs (those would require an additional NDA amendment).

-Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@aurorafin.com>, AuroraFin Security <security@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: BYO escrow & cross-region rotation artifacts — package attached

Hi Lena — attaching the requested artifacts. Summary of what's included below and short answers to the assessor's likely follow-ups.

Attachments:
- byok-escrow-letter-signed.pdf (signed BYO acceptance; includes signer and date)
- rotation-runbook.pdf (detailed steps and automated hooks used during rotation)
- kms-operator-shiftlog.csv (redacted operator shift slice with signed digest)

Quick clarifications:
- Rotation timeline: the rotation executed 2028-10-29T22:01:12Z with staggered rewraps across eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; automated health checks allowed zero customer-facing downtime. The runbook documents the exact replay commands and the TTL used for KV cache flush.
- Escrow: BYO escrow letter confirms acceptance of key wrapping artifacts; private key material was not exchanged — only wrapped key blobs and a signed manifest were handed over.
- Integrity: each shiftlog row has a SHA256 checksum and we include a PGP-signed audit digest file (in-runbook appendix) to prove non-repudiation.

If the assessor needs the notarized letter or a timestamping authority stamp, we can request time-stamp authority output (ETA +3 business days). Also can provide an MD5/SHA1 parity file if required.

Thanks — reach out if anything else is needed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
